dedupe_keys.name: u s cropland conversion 2008 2016 lark and others 2020 30 m conversion maps and yield differentials

description: This dataset maps cropland change across the conterminous United States at 30 m for 2008 to 2016. The Zenodo record says a geodatabase classifies land as stable non-cropland, stable cropland, cropland expansion, cropland abandonment or intermittent cropland, with layers for the year converted to or from cropland and the land cover before first and after last crop in Cropland Data Layer classes, plus local and national yield differential maps for corn, soybeans and wheat. It was published in June 2020 (version 1.0.0) by researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the CC BY 4.0 licence, free to download as a zipped ESRI geodatabase of about 770 MB and a yield file. Coverage is the conterminous United States. Caveats: intermittent classes may reflect rotations or classifier confusion. For simulation it gives where farmland is expanding or being abandoned to update agricultural exposure and land use scenarios. Related catalogue records include the USDA Cropland Data Layer and the Corn Soy Data Layer for the US Midwest.
